title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Problem (Case IV, §35): find all transverse vibrations of an elastic rod (Euler–Bernoulli beam) whose two ends are both 'simply fixed' (pinned, simply supported). The boundary conditions are y=0 and y''=0 at s=0 and at s=a. The spatial factor is α e^{s/f}+β e^{-s/f}+γ sin(s/f)+δ cos(s/f). The conditions at s=0 give β=-α and δ=0. With ω=a/f, the conditions at s=a give α=0 and γ sin ω=0. A nontrivial motion therefore requires sin ω=0, so ω=nπ exactly. ω=0 is rest. ω=π gives the fundamental. Since frequency ∝ ω², the partials are π c√(2gb)/a² × (1, 4, 9, 16, ...); in Euler's convention this counts simple (half) vibrations per second, i.e. the time argument ω²c√(2gb)/a² divided by π. The musical labels follow from the ratios. 4 is two octaves (c̄). 9 = 8·9/8 is three octaves plus a major second (d). 16 is four octaves (c). 25 = 16·25/16 is four octaves plus a 5-limit augmented fifth (gis). 36 = 32·9/8 is five octaves plus a major second (d). The general motion is the superposition y = Σ C^{(n)} sin(ζ^{(n)} + t n²π² c√(2gb)/a²) sin(nπ s/a). §36: the n-th mode is a sine curve, identical in shape to the string's n-th mode, with n−1 interior nodes; the fundamental has the shape of the simple string vibration. The next page compares the fundamentals of the four end-condition cases treated so far.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The eigenvalue condition, the n² frequency law and the mode shapes sin(nπs/a) are correct for the pinned–pinned Euler–Bernoulli beam.
Minor wording slip in §36: for the second mode Euler writes 'figura chordae' where the rod (virga) is meant. He is referring to the identical sine shape.
Previous page has a typographical 'sin. α ω' for 'sin. ω' in the second reduced equation. It is harmless.

ideas.what: Exact eigenvalues ω=nπ for the simply supported beam; frequencies proportional to n²
ideas.modern_name: Natural frequencies of the pinned–pinned Euler–Bernoulli beam, ω_n ∝ (nπ/L)²√(EI/ρA)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526, 1779/1782); recounted by Truesdell 1960 and later Rayleigh
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Mode shapes sin(nπs/a), identical to string modes, with n−1 nodes
ideas.modern_name: Sine eigenfunctions of the fourth-order operator with hinged boundary conditions

ideas.what: General motion as an infinite superposition of simple modes with arbitrary amplitudes and phases
ideas.modern_name: Modal expansion / principle of superposition (Fourier sine series in space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (strings, 1753); Euler's use for beams is noted by Truesdell

ideas.what: Musical identification of the partials 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 in 5-limit just intonation; remark that the n² series is more 'harmonious' than the string's n series
ideas.modern_name: Inharmonic (here, sparse harmonic) overtone series of bars
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; later Chladni's acoustic studies of bars

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard, correctly solved pinned–pinned beam case. It is well documented as Euler's in the history of elasticity (Truesdell). The musical labelling is a known feature of this paper.
transcription_corrections: Note series (image): C, c, d, c, gis, d with increasing overbars. The bars correspond to 2, 3, 4, 4, 5 octaves above C; the transcription's '[?]' marks can be resolved as gis (25) and d (36).
Third term in the image indeed reads √(2bg) rather than √(2gb). It is equivalent and not an error.
Margin note 'Tab. III. Fig. 1.' belongs to §36.
